source.title: Intrinsic dimensionality and generalization properties of the R-norm inductive bias
source.authors: Navid Ardeshir; Daniel J. Hsu; C. Sanford

record.tranche_reason: The paper proves that minimum-R-norm interpolants can generalize poorly on sampled parity data, qualifying claims that weight-based inductive bias alone ensures good generalization. It does not test the specific settings in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The paper gives theoretical results for R-norm-minimizing interpolants on parity and periodic ridge-function datasets. The parity generalization bounds are recorded below. Its structural bounds on R-norm and width, and results cited from prior work, do not measure a version in the claim.
record.test_reason: The study proves generalization bounds for minimum-R-norm parity interpolants, but none of its results test V1–V8. Statistical suboptimality of this inductive bias does not contradict any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: minimum-R-norm interpolation can favor multidirectional functions over ridge interpolants and has statistically suboptimal sample complexity for parity learning. The authors leave a gap between their lower and upper sample-complexity bounds.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes solutions to an explicit R-norm-minimization variational problem, rather than networks trained with standard gradient methods on natural labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Target function and sample size affect the generalization result: for parity, the paper gives a poor-generalization lower bound below n = o(d^2 / log d) and a clipped-error upper bound for n ≥ C(log(1/δ) + d^3/ϵ^2).

fits_no_version.finding: Minimum-R-norm parity interpolants have nearly trivial L2 prediction error at small sample sizes; sufficiently large samples guarantee small squared L2 error after clipping.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For uniformly sampled d-variable parity, if n = o(d²/√(log d)), every minimum-R-norm interpolant has L2 error at least 1 − o(1) with probability at least 1/2. Theorem 9 guarantees clipped squared L2 error at most ε when n ≥ C(log(1/δ) + d³/ε²), with probability at least 1 − δ.

record.problems: The results are theoretical and specific to parity and R-norm-minimizing interpolants. The lower and upper sample-complexity bounds differ by roughly a factor of d log d, which the authors identify as an unresolved gap.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were omitted that measure a version in the claim. Structural interpolation bounds and results on periodic ridge-function targets do not measure the listed versions.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization versus natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Theoretical guarantees are valid findings but do not establish any listed version. R-norm is not magnitude-aware sharpness, and representational width bounds do not measure the effect of widening on test error.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fitting random labels, natural labels, standard gradient training, or the named architectures.
Does not sweep network width past the zero-training-error threshold or measure test error across width.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected architectures on image datasets.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD or measure held-out performance under optimizer tuning.
Does not vary batch size or compare training budgets.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with generalization gaps.
Does not remove memorized examples and measure the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: every solution to (VP) for the sampled parity dataset
rows.size_stated: two-layer ReLU neural network; width not fixed
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical bound on the generalization error of solutions minimizing R-norm subject to fitting sampled parity data exactly.
rows.value: With probability at least 1/2, every solution has error at least 1 − o(1).
rows.uncertainty: Probability at least 1/2; asymptotic bound as stated.
rows.note: The result concerns parity and an R-norm minimizer, not standard gradient training on natural labels.
rows.check: The sample-size condition is n = o(d²/√(log d)), not o(d²/log d). The displaced radical in Theorem 7 is confirmed by its proof, which sets α = 64n√(ln d)/d². The error bound and probability are correctly recorded. The zero predictor has L2 error 1, providing the trivial-error reference. This theorem measures no listed version, so observed is not an applicable version-relative state.

rows.note: The upper bound is for clipped predictions and leaves a gap of roughly a factor of d log d from the lower bound.
